findings.where: crates/engine/src/cmd/ai_cmds/generate.rs:71 (dpi taken from the open document) and :103-106 (file.new in the apply step)
findings.issue: Generate Image into a new document copies the open document's resolution into `file.new`, which refuses any resolution outside 1..=30000 ppi (document_preset_cmds::validate_new_params). Imported documents can hold such resolutions: PSD (psd_import.rs:1175 takes ResolutionInfo unclamped, including 0), XCF (up to 1e6), Pigment 0.1-0.4 files (legacy_pigment/mod.rs:484, up to 1e6); Image Size keeps the document's own value. The refusal happens in the job's apply step, after the provider has answered, so the request is billed and the image is thrown away.
findings.scenario: Open a PSD whose resolution resource says 40000 ppi (or 0). Edit > Generate Image..., New document, any prompt (or `pigment-cli run hi.psd --cmd ai.generateImage --params '{"prompt":"a magenta box","target":"document","width":64,"height":64}' --allow-ai`). Verified here with target/debug/pigment-cli against a 127.0.0.1 mock of OpenAI: the 300 ppi PSD gives {"document":1,...}; the 40000 ppi PSD sends the same GET /v1/models and POST /v1/images/generations, then fails with "`ai.generateImage`: invalid parameters for `file.new`: `resolution` must be a number within 1..=30000". Nothing lands.
findings.test: In ai_cmds/tests.rs: rgb(32, 32), then s.edit(|doc, _| { doc.resolution_dpi = 40000.0; Ok(()) }); install a connected, consented MockBackend with one Solid answer; execute ai.generateImage {prompt, target:"document", width:64, height:64}. Today: Err and mock.calls().len() == 1. With the fix: Ok, a second document whose resolution is 30000 (or 72), one call. Repeat with 0.0 and f32::NAN.
findings.fix: Before `prepare`, make the new document's resolution valid: `let dpi = open.map(|(..,dpi,_)| f64::from(dpi)).filter(|d| d.is_finite()).map_or(72.0, |d| d.clamp(1.0, MAX_RESOLUTION));` (or 72 when out of range). More generally, anything the apply step passes to another command must be validated before the request is sent, since apply runs after billing.

findings.where: crates/engine/src/jobs.rs:689-693 (independent_of_document lets every `view.` command through) with :2060-2063 (apply discards on any change of the document Arc); reached from ai_cmds fill.rs:109, expand.rs:82, generate.rs:84, background.rs:230
findings.issue: The document lock an AI request takes (decision 6) does not hold for the `view.*` commands that edit the Document itself: view.newGuide, moveGuide, editGuide, deleteGuide, clearGuides, clearCanvasGuides, clearSelectedArtboardGuides, newGuideLayout, newGuidesFromShape, setRulerOrigin, resetRulerOrigin, clearSlices, lockSlices. They pass job_conflict because of the `view.` prefix, run Session::edit (guides, slices and the ruler origin live in Document), and replace the document Arc. When the paid answer arrives, apply_job sees a different Arc and discards it: "the document changed while it ran; the result was discarded". Undo is guarded for the same reason (session/history.rs:14), so the hole is not intended.
findings.scenario: Make a selection, Edit > Generative Fill... with a real provider (10 to 60 s). While the status bar shows the request, choose View > Guides > New Guide... and add a guide (or New Guide Layout, or set the ruler origin). The request finishes and is billed; the job ends as failed and no layer lands.
findings.test: Engine test: rgb(64, 64), select a rect, MockBackend with set_delay(300 ms) and one Solid answer; s.start("ai.generativeFill", {prompt}) -> Job; then s.execute("view.newGuide", {orientation:"vertical", position:10}). Today it returns Ok and, after waiting for the job, the job outcome is Failed with "changed while it ran" while mock.calls().len() == 1. With the fix, view.newGuide is refused as Disabled ("still running on this document") and the fill lands as one step.
findings.fix: Narrow independent_of_document to the view commands that do not edit the Document (zoom, fit, proof, gamut, colour samplers that live in DocState), or have job_conflict refuse the listed guide, slice and ruler-origin ids while a locking job runs on the active document. An alternative for the AI jobs alone: in their apply, accept a document whose layers, canvas and selection are unchanged (compare those, not the Arc).

findings.where: crates/engine/src/cmd/ai_cmds/fill.rs:46-51 (the `?` on call and check_answer inside the variations loop)
findings.issue: With 2 or 3 variations, each variation is a separate billed request. If a later one fails (a 429 rate limit, a safety block, a timeout, a wrong-size answer), the `?` ends the whole job and the variations already received and paid for are dropped; nothing lands.
findings.scenario: Generative Fill with Variations 3. The first two requests succeed; the third returns a rate-limit or safety error (likely on quick successive image requests). The job fails with the third request's message, the document is unchanged and two paid images are lost.
findings.test: MockBackend connected, push Solid, Solid, Error(quota); select a rect; execute ai.generativeFill {prompt, variations:3}. Today: Err, mock.calls().len() == 3, layer count unchanged. With the fix: two layers "Generative Fill 1" and "2" in one undo step, and the result (or the job's message) says the third failed and why.
findings.fix: Collect the successful variations; on a non-cancel error after at least one success, stop asking and land what arrived (one step), returning the error alongside (for example `{"layers":[...],"failed":{"kind","message"}}`) so the window can show it. Cancel keeps discarding everything, as documented.

findings.where: crates/engine/src/cmd/ai_cmds/background.rs:243-246 and :269 (provider Remove Background); fill.rs:163-167 (visible_alpha for Generate Background)
findings.issue: Remove Background with AI Provider promises a mask "within the layer's existing mask", but reads the old mask with LayerMask::values_into, which applies density and ignores the mask's feather, then replaces the mask with `LayerMask { surface, ..LayerMask::reveal_all() }`: feather 0, linked true. A feathered mask's soft edge is baked in hard, and an unlinked mask becomes linked. Generate Background's subject (visible_alpha) uses the same unfeathered values.
findings.scenario: A pixel layer with a layer mask hiding its left half, Properties > Feather 20 px (a soft transition), mask unlinked. Layer > Remove Background with AI Provider; the provider returns the subject covering the whole layer. Expected: the soft 20 px transition stays. Actual: the transition becomes a hard edge at the old mask boundary, the Feather setting reads 0 and the mask is linked again.
findings.test: rgb(64, 32), add a mask whose left 32 columns are 0, set feather = 16 and linked = false; MockBackend answering Solid [10, 10, 10, 255] (opaque and dark, so key_white_border keys nothing and the whole layer is the subject). Run ai.removeBackground {method:"provider"}; compare the composite at x = 24..40 with the composite before: today it jumps from hidden to shown between columns 31 and 32 (before, it was a ramp), mask.feather == 0 and mask.linked == true.
findings.fix: Read what the old mask shows as the compositor draws it (feather applied, e.g. through photocraft_compose's mask sampling, or blur the values with the mask's feather as compose does) when computing `shown`, and keep the old mask's `linked` (and `enabled`) when building the new one. Use the same values in visible_alpha.

checked:
Read FORK.md, PKG-ai-P1.md, PKG-ai-review123.md and PKG-ai-final.md (known items not repeated). Read all of crates/engine/src/cmd/ai_cmds.rs and ai_cmds/{fill,expand,generate,background,describe,region}.rs, generative.rs and generative/mock.rs, and traced them through jobs::run/new_job/apply_job/finish_job_step, job_conflict and independent_of_document, Session::edit (sampler/symmetry maps, colour restriction), dispatch/admit, actions recording (recorded, replayable, after_command's nested-journal truncation), batch_run's playing counter and scratch sessions, actions.recordAgain, Script Events (file_menu.firing), Quick Mask, layer.removeBackground (cutout_cmds), file.new validation, image.canvasSize/translate_doc, LayerMask, Surface::content_bounds/from_interleaved/write_interleaved, and the app's AppBackend admit and automation genai.rs.
Found sound: nothing is sent before the backend, consent, provider fit, prompt and document checks, and every refusal (no selection, Quick Mask, no sky or subject, nothing to expand) happens before the request; actions, batches (named, nested or with scratch sessions that have no backend), droplets and script events never send; recordAgain and scripts an agent reaches are held by admit(automated); unrecorded/may_send agree with run() for every method value; Generate Image's nested file.new is not recorded into an action; pixel helpers cannot panic on any input (clamp bounds, cover_to/pad_to_aspect subtractions, interleaved lengths all match the rect); answers are size-checked; one undo step per command (Expand's canvas growth and layer together; Remove Background's Background conversion inside the same edit; sampler map consumed by that edit); Expand keeps the document id; the provider Remove Background mask hides outside the sent rect (from_interleaved default 0), so opaque-default Backgrounds (Affinity, Krita) mask correctly; alpha channels, layer-mask targets and colour restriction do not route ai.* commands; undo and journaled commands are refused while a request runs; cancel drops answers; ai.status never shows more than four characters of a hint.
Verified end to end with target/debug/pigment-cli and a 127.0.0.1 mock (scripts in scratchpad/hunt-ai/scripts): AIE-1 reproduces exactly as described. No cargo was run.
